newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat rises further as dry weather continues.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat rises further as dry weather continues.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures continued to rise on Tuesday under the influence of dry conditions in Australia's eastern wheatbelt.

Turnover was moderately heavy, with 29 contracts changing hands. Unusually, buying interest spilled beyond market leader January 1998 to the more distant May, July, November 1998 and January 1999 contracts.
January 1998 sold 50 cents higher at A$201.00, with 21 contracts changing hands. May 1998 sold A$4.00 higher at A$204.50 while July 1998 traded up by A$5.50 to A$208.50.
November 1998 and January 1999 both sold A$7.00 a tonne lower, at A$205.50 and A$200.00 respectively.
Settlement prices mostly rose by about A$6.00 a tonne.
January 1998 also attracted 13 put option trades, at A$190.00 and A$195.00 a tonne, on premiums of A$7.00 and A$9.00 respectively.
Kerrin Gleeson of Elders Risk Management said the market reflected Australia's continuing dry conditions.
